speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; tell me, does this happen when you are fully awake and aware of your surroundings, or does it start while you are asleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus. 

The patient's history of recurrent staring spells, unresponsiveness, post-ictal lethargy, and specific automatisms (hand gestures, grimacing) strongly suggests this diagnosis. As a 7-year-old with these semiological features, he likely has underlying Childhood Absence Epilepsy that has progressed to a non-convulsive status. 

To confirm the diagnosis and assess severity, I request an EEG and a brain MRI.
